title: EIP-8189: snap/2 - BAL-Based State Healing
description: Replaces trie node healing with block access list based state catch-up in the snap protocol
author: Toni Wahrstätter (@nerolation), Gary Rong (@rjl493456442)
laymanDescription: Speeds up node syncing. Today a syncing node chases down missing pieces of state one request at a time. This lets it instead download the record of what each block changed and apply those changes in order, so the remaining work is known upfront.
benefits: Replaces iterative trie node discovery with a known, upfront set of block diffs
Reduces round trips during the snap sync catch-up phase
Removes the need to maintain a separate trie healing mechanism
Allows recovery from reorgs past the pivot without restarting sync
tradeoffs: Requires rolling out a new protocol version; older peers stay on snap/1
Only usable for post-Glamsterdam blocks within the BAL retention period
Serving peers must retain orphaned block BALs to support reorg recovery
